title: Walks that drag a clip on the timeline by window point really move it
goal: Several walks drag clips, sound levels and fade handles on the timeline by posting a mouse drag to the window, and pass without checking the result. On 2026-09-26 one of them was shown to move nothing at all, so those walks report green on gestures they never performed.
notes: Reproduced 2026-09-26. Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/a-clip-s-sound-is-linked-under-it-walk.json --no-build -> 'walk complete', but 2-sound-dragged-sc.png shows Tutorial Sample still starting at 0s after step 'windowDrag from [691,943] to [864,943]' (should have slid about 1.5s). Separately, a probe walk with Select in hand did windowDrag from [907,854] to [1042,854] on a b-roll clip at 8s (clip's lane measured off the -sc.png of a 1728x990pt window) and expectClip startsAt 10 failed: b-roll still 8.00s to 16.00s. The window is kept invisible during walks (capture log: 'the window was still invisible, so it was shown for the one shot'); a theory, not confirmed, is that NSApp.postEvent to an ordered-out window never reaches SwiftUI hit testing. PlaytestHarness.swift case .windowDrag posts mouseMoved/Down/Dragged/Up via NSApp.postEvent. Other users of windowDrag: keys-copy-between-layers-walk, timeline-right-click-walk. The track-select-forward walk sidestepped it with a new dragClip step that drives EditorState like dragTiming does.
acceptance: A windowDrag on a timeline clip in a walk moves that clip, and the walk claims where it landed with expectClip
a-clip-s-sound-is-linked-under-it-walk fails if its sound drag moves nothing
Every walk using windowDrag on the timeline either claims the result or is rewritten onto a step that drives the editor

log.note: A rightClick step at the same window point [907,854] did reach b-roll's clip menu (16 rows, Select Forward chosen and it worked), so the point maps onto the clip; it is the posted drag that does not reach it.

triage 2026-09-26: posted left clicks on the timeline stopped answering in the same window (see clicking-a-cut-opens-the-transition-picker-again, p1). The drag that moves nothing may be the same cause; check this again once that lands before rewriting walks.

2026-09-26: re-check before working this. It was found while a 'Photonz (Probe) quit unexpectedly' dialog held the front (2026-09-25 23:22 to 09-26 ~12:50Z), which kept the probe from ever being active; a window that is not key takes no synthesized event on a SwiftUI gesture, which is exactly 'posted windowDrags never reach timeline clips'. Taps on the timeline recovered the moment the dialog closed (clicking-a-cut-opens-the-transition-picker-again). Run the drag walk again with the Grants line clean before building anything.

triage 2026-09-27: e459d903 (walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-5) now takes the front for every real drag, so a posted windowDrag should move the clip again. What is left is the other half: every timeline windowDrag walk claims where the thing landed, so a drag that moves nothing can never pass.

Re-ran a-clip-s-sound-is-linked-under-it-walk with the Grants line clean: the posted sound drag DOES move the clip now (0.00s -> 0.86s), since e459d903 takes the front for real drags. But two of its drags were still silently wrong: key cmd+z never undid (the menu bar is frozen in a background probe), so the fade drag at x=110 missed the clip (it started at 0.86s) and moved the playhead instead; Fade in stayed 0.0s.

Fixed: every timeline windowDrag in the three walks now claims its result. Sound walk: expectClip after each clip drag (moved, undone, detached sound alone), expect field 'Volume reading' -9.3 dB, 'Fade in' 0.7s; undo via shortcut menuItem Undo. Right-click walk: expectTimeline playheadMS after each ruler drag, plus hasIn/hasOut/markers; its note said Out at six but x=1119 is 5.04s, corrected to five. Keys walk: new expectLevel step (points, dipsBelowDB, flat; PhotonzCore parse + tests, harness reads layer.soundLevel) claims the three level points, the dip and the undo. Proof the claim bites: a scratch copy with the first sound drag made a no-op failed '[13 expectClip] FAILED: no clip called Tutorial Sample is starting at 0.86s'.

Found and filed: key cmd+z in a background probe often runs nothing (keys walk's 'one undo puts the whole drag back' test never undid: dip stayed -60.5 dB). Filed a-walk-s-command-z-undoes-what-it-says-or-the-wa (p2) with the survey of 18 walks. No audit: this is walk-harness work, nothing a person sees in the app changed.

Every timeline windowDrag in the three walks that use it now claims its result (expectClip, expect Volume reading/Fade in, expectTimeline, new expectLevel step with core tests). Verified: all three walks pass; a copy with the sound drag made a no-op fails at expectClip. Found key cmd+z runs no menu in a background probe (two walks were silently not undoing), switched them to the Undo shortcut step, filed a-walk-s-command-z-undoes-what-it-says-or-the-wa. Scripts/test.sh green (10261 tests). Commits 01fc24b8 + progress log.
